### Castor
- **Baseline:** **Cozy** is the SMT-based comparator mentioned in the Castor paper.
- **Why SMT limits it:** The paper says that “**the size of the TPC-H queries causes a significant slowdown in its solver-based verification step**.” So the SMT-based verification step becomes too slow on large queries.
- **Main result against it:** Castor outperformed Cozy on the TPC-H benchmarks; the paper says Cozy was effective on small specifications, but on TPC-H, “**Q4 was slower than baseline Hyper at 5.4s and Q17 was too slow to run on the entire TPC-H dataset**.”

### Hectare
- **Baseline:** **Hoogle+** is the SMT-based baseline.
- **Why SMT limits it:** The paper describes Hoogle+ as “**based on an SMT encoding of Petri-net reachability**,” and the evaluation indicates this approach does poorly as search problems get larger and more complex. In the new benchmark suite, the original Hoogle+ “**cannot solve any of the new benchmarks**,” and even the expanded variant performs poorly because “**adding nullary versions of all components blows up the Petri net and makes the reachability problem intractable**.”
- **Main result against it:** Hectare “**solves 88% of synthesis problems in the combined benchmark suite compared to only 64% by Hoogle+**,” and on commonly solved benchmarks it is “**8× faster on average**.” On the newly collected benchmarks, Hectare solves **13 out of 19**, while HplusAll solves only **3 out of 19**.
